title: Harry Ransom Center opens new exhibition: The Worlds of Gertrude Stein
summary: The Harry Ransom Center at The University of Texas at Austin presents The Worlds of Gertrude Stein, an interdisciplinary exhibition examining the life and writing of Gertrude Stein, a legendary but much misunderstood modernist figure. Opening August 15, 2026, and running through January 11, 2027, this exhibition is organized by guest curator Dr. Sophie Oliver, Senior Lecturer in Modernism at the University of Liverpool. The exhibition explores three intersecting worlds that Gertrude Stein inhabited: the everyday world of her home, the creative world of words which she made so distinctively her own, and the public world where she found fame. Reflecting on home and belonging, on insiders and outsiders, on the thirst for fame and the desire for privacy, the exhibition invites visitors to reconsider the complexities and contradictions of a literary icon.

title: Prince of Prints: The Pucci story, now in an updated edition with new photography
summary: Emilio Pucci had a passion for women, a visionary sense of style, and an eye for color and design. With these talents, he created a fashion house unlike any other. By the early ’50s, his boutique on the isle of Capri was catering to wealthy sophisticates, heiresses, and movie stars buying his “Capri pants,” silk scarves, and lightweight separates. By the end of the decade, Jacqueline Kennedy and Marilyn Monroe were wearing his dresses, and by the mid-’60s, the label was synonymous with the gilded lifestyle of an international jetset. The Pucci story is a modern epic with its roots in renaissance Italy: the brand’s founder, the Marchese Emilio Pucci di Barsento, was a charismatic aristocrat whose lineage extends back to the 15th century. It is a story of evolution: a family company that grew from one tiny store to an international brand. title: Galerie Barbara Thumm to present fourth solo exhibition by Carrie Mae Weems
summary: Galerie Barbara Thumm announce their fourth exhibition with the outstanding American Artist Carrie Mae Weems (*1953, Portland OR, US), one of the most influential voices in contemporary art today. Over a career spanning more than four decades, Weems has created a complex and multifaceted body of work encompassing photography, film, installation and other media, while engaging with the social and political issues of the present which continue to shape our world today. The exhibition will open concurrently with Weems’s travelling exhibition Carrie Mae Weems: The Heart of the Matter at C/O Berlin during Berlin Art Week 2026, as part of a series of events celebrating her work. In the series Seaside, Weems revisits her now-iconic strategy of self-portraiture as witness. Photographed from behind on a single beach, the artist appears in moments of quiet reverie facing the ocean’s horizon. Seated at an easel, she attempts to render the vast and unknowable

title: Matisse exhibition at SFMOMA reunites works from iconic 1905 Paris Salon
summary: Henri Matisse ignited passionate controversy in 1905 with the public debut of Femme au chapeau (Woman with a Hat) at the Salon d’Automne in Paris. The portrait of the artist’s wife, Amélie, was at the center of a defining moment of rupture in the history of modern art, shocking audiences with its seemingly carefree brushstrokes and bright hues that purposefully departed from observed reality. It was established as the leading image of Fauvism, the first French avant-garde art movement of the 20th century. Until September 13, 2026, the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art presents Matisse’s Femme au chapeau: A Modern Scandal, a major exhibition illuminating how the painting—now an icon of the museum’s collection—made its mark on art history. title: Friedrichs Pontone gallery opens international summer group exhibition
summary: Friedrichs Pontone announced the opening of their summer exhibition, showcasing a selection of works from across the gallery's roster. The Summer Show brings together exceptional new and established talent from the US, UK, Canada, South Korea and Estonia, blending together contemporary voices in abstraction, figuration and mixed media installation. Born in 1983, Chris Rivers is a self taught artist from Manchester, England. His large and dramatic oil paintings are bold, abstract displays of charged colour and fine, surrealistic detail. Not everything is as it first seems in these worlds. Soft light filters through overlaying mists of complimentary tones, gradually swelling with dramatic saturated colour before receding into the image. Estonian artist Kristi Kongi makes paintings and site-specific installations. title: Lisson Gallery presents group exhibition Past Presence in London
summary: Lisson London introduces a group exhibition of works by artists from its international programme, including Dana Awartani, Rodney Graham, Peter Joseph, Anish Kapoor, Wael Shawky, Hiroshi Sugimoto, Tunga, and Masaomi Yasunaga – united by their collision of the past and present. The exhibition derives its name from Hiroshi Sugimoto’s acclaimed series, Past Presence, where masterworks are transformed into reflections on cultural continuity, memory and time. Two pieces from the series are highlighted, preceding the artist’s forthcoming solo show at Lisson New York and the reopening of the Hirshhorn Museum Sculpture Garden later this year. Acting as the entry point to the exhibition is Past Presence 042, No. 3 / No. 13, Mark Rothko (2014), a black-and-white photograph of an early Rothko composition at MoMA, New York, paired with Past Presence 077, The Big Ear, Alexander Calder (2016), captured at Basel’s Fondation Beyeler. title: De Young presents Superficial Matters highlighting Bay Area artists
summary: Superficial Matters: Artists from the Svane Gift and Beyond continues the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco’s series of exhibitions drawn from a major acquisition of 42 artworks by 30 emerging and midcareer Bay Area artists and collectives, supported by a $1 million gift of the Svane Family Foundation. Following the inaugural Crafting Radicality: Bay Area Artists from the Svane Gift in 2023 and About Place: Bay Area Artists from the Svane Gift in 2024, Superficial Matters: Artists from the Svane Gift and Beyond marks the third iteration in the series. The exhibition highlights eight artists who mine the material possibilities of their chosen mediums—from ceramics to photography to painting—to explore the surfaces of bodies and objects as critical sites of identity formation. title: SFMOMA appoints Anna Katz as Senior Curator and Head of Painting and Sculpture
summary: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art announced the appointment of Anna Katz as the Doris and Donald Fisher Senior Curator and Head of Painting and Sculpture. She will be the first person to hold the position since it was recently endowed by the Fisher family in honor of Doris and Donald Fisher’s deep love of art and artists and decades-long investment in SFMOMA. Katz joins SFMOMA from the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles (MOCA), where she most recently served as senior curator. She will begin in her position at SFMOMA on August 17, 2026. In her new role, Katz will work closely with Christopher Bedford, Helen and Charles Schwab Director, and Janet Bishop, Thomas Weisel Family Chief Curator, in tandem with the full Department of Painting and Sculpture staff, to develop the vision for the department and guide its exhibition and acquisition strategies going forward. title: INAH releases new publication on relocation of Mexico's archaeological monuments
summary: Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) has presented a new publication examining one of the most complex questions facing archaeological preservation today: what happens when protecting cultural heritage requires moving it from its original location. Titled Cultural Heritage and Development: The Relocation of Archaeological Monuments in Mexico, the digital volume brings together the work of 18 specialists and grew out of a series of academic discussions organized by INAH around the relocation of pre-Hispanic remains, including archaeological interventions carried out during construction of the Maya Train. The book was presented during the 37th International Anthropology and History Book Fair (FILAH), held at Mexico City’s National Museum of Anthropology. title: Schoelkopf Gallery exhibits photorealist Richard Estes' standalone photographs
summary: This summer, Schoelkopf Gallery presents Richard Estes: My Camera Is My Sketchbook, offering a revealing look into the practice of one of the leading figures in photorealist art. The exhibition focuses on scenes from New York City and Maine, locations where Estes has lived, worked, and found inspiration for many years. Notably, this exhibition will present photographs by Estes as standalone artworks for the first time in the artist's career. Estes has taken photographs as reference material for decades, but in this exhibition, he presents photographs as artworks unto themselves for the first time. The Schoelkopf Gallery exhibition follows recent notable institutional presentations of Estes' work including Richard Estes: Urban Landscapes at the Portland Museum of Art in Maine (2021), Richard Estes: Voyages at the Newport Street Gallery in London (2021), and Richard Estes: Painting New York City at the

title: Pilar Corrias presents exhibition of new paintings by Hayv Kahraman
summary: Pilar Corrias is presenting What cannot be said will be wept, an exhibition of new paintings by Hayv Kahraman. The exhibition draws on Kahraman’s personal history as a Kurdish-Iraqi refugee and the loss of her home in the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires to consider the effects of systems that separate people from land, ancestry, ecology and embodied forms of knowledge. The artist's text, written to accompany the exhibition, is included in full below: One of the deepest spells modernity has cast upon me is that of separation. Yes, I was extracted from my land through systemic violence, occupation and domination, this is one form of rupture. But there is another, more insidious severing I am only now beginning to name: a disconnection from my environment, from the natural world, from the human and more-than-human and from a kind of knowing behind knowing. title: Garrison Art Center presents Rising Tide exhibition by Julie Harrison
summary: Garrison Art Center presents Rising Tide, a solo exhibition of twelve works on paper made over the past four years by visual artist and educator Julie Harrison. Driven by curiosity and adventure, Harrison has spent her career investigating materials to mine their visual and physical attributes, playing with changing forms of expression and experimenting with the new. This process has guided the evolution of her work over the years, moving from early video art and performance into drawing. “My work explores invisible structures that shape organic life and ecological systems,” said Harrison, “I visually interpret this through layered, abstract lines and shapes that map energetic exchanges to construct fragments of an imagined biology. title: UNESCO delivers report from the Reactive Monitoring Mission to Calakmul
summary: UNESCO has concluded that there are currently no grounds to consider placing the Ancient Maya City and Protected Tropical Forests of Calakmul on the List of World Heritage in Danger, following an assessment of the impact of Mexico's Maya Train project on the internationally recognized site. The finding is contained in a report from a Reactive Monitoring Mission delivered by UNESCO's World Heritage Centre to Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) and the National Commission of Natural Protected Areas (Conanp). Located in the state of Campeche, Calakmul is one of the most significant Maya archaeological sites in Mexico and forms part of an extensive tropical forest ecosystem. title: Harwood Museum of Art opens major adobe exhibition Unearthing Futures
summary: Unearthing Futures / Desenterrando Futuros explores adobe as a living practice linking art, architecture, and ancestral knowledge across the Americas. Bringing together artists Gabriel Chaile, rafa esparza, Santino Gonzales, Joanna Keane Lopez, Ronald Rael, and Christine Howard Sandoval, the exhibition examines how earth, water, and fiber, shaped by hand and sustained through communal care, embody both tradition and transformation. At an unprecedented scale for Harwood Museum of Art, the exhibition physically transforms the building through monumental, site-responsive installations. Galleries are reconfigured by large-scale adobe structures, architectural interventions, and immersive environments that alter circulation, sightlines, and the spatial experience of the museum itself. title: Artist Jacob Hashimoto to unveil largest-ever artwork
summary: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art launches Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc, the largest installation of the multimedia artist’s career, with a public celebration on August 20, 2026. Mixing nearly 75,000 hand-built kites made of bamboo and Japanese paper suspended together into a cloud canopy, the site-specific exhibition will cover the museum’s ground floor admission-free Roberts Family Gallery from floor to ceiling and wall to wall. “Our mission at SFMOMA is radical hospitality for all—these efforts include filling over 45,000 square feet of free public space with irresistible contemporary art,” said Christopher Bedford, Helen and Charles Schwab Director of SFMOMA. “Jacob Hashimoto’s enveloping and breathtaking commission in our free-to-visit Roberts Family Gallery promises to welcome visitors of all ages, imbuing all who experience it

title: Major exhibition explores the living art of West African masquerade
summary: The Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg is presenting New African Masquerades: Artistic Innovations and Collaborations, on view from August 15, 2026, through January 3, 2027. Bringing together thirteen intricate, full-body masquerade ensembles alongside photography, video, and immersive multimedia experiences, the exhibition offers a rare introduction to contemporary masquerade traditions and artistic conversations across West Africa. New Masquerades: Artistic Innovations and Collaborations is organized by the New Orleans Museum of Art, in partnership with the Museé des Civilisations noires in Dakar, Senegal, and received generous support from the National Endowment for the Humanities. title: NıCOLETTı gallery presents Patent 3306x by Appau Jnr Boakye-Yiadom
summary: NıCOLETTı is presenting Patent 3306x, a solo exhibition by London-based artist Appau Jnr Boakye-Yiadom (b. 1984). Patent 3306x follows Boakye-Yiadom’s three-year research as the inaugural recipient of the Donna Lynas Residency (2023–26), a partnership between Wysing Arts Centre, Modern Art Oxford, Somerset House and South London Gallery. During the residency, the artist developed a series of exhibitions informed by his study of musical instruments in the Bate Collection at Oxford University and the Pitt Rivers Museum, Oxford. Its final chapter, Modular Merger, is currently on view at Modern Art Oxford until 13 September 2026. Working across installation, painting, video and photography, Boakye-Yiadom examines the systems through which objects, images and knowledge are classified, circulated and assigned value. title: Palmer Gallery presents an exhibition of paintings by Charlotte Winifred Guérard
summary: Cherry, cherry brings together paintings Charlotte Winifred Guérard made between the Royal Academy Schools studios (summer 2025) and the Hampshire countryside (Xenia residency, spring 2026). Each work is an abstraction that responds to Guérard's inner worlds - shades of thoughts, distant memories, and more tangible experiences of life meet on the canvas. The title, Cherry, cherry, captures the feeling of jumping from spring to summer, when persistent, piercing light enhances the colours around us - a temporal shift echoed by the lazy, heat-imbued mood of JJ Cale's "Cherry”, which influenced Guérard at the time. The show stages a dialogue between materiality and external observation. title: Sensory overload makes it harder for female treefrogs to select a mate
summary: When shopping for a new appliance, choosing a movie to watch or even ordering a cup of coffee, people often experience “choice overload.” New research from the Smithsonian suggests that female Cope’s gray treefrogs face a similar challenge when selecting a mate. In a study published today in iScience, researchers from the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute and the University of Tennessee found that when female treefrogs are confronted with too many males calls at once, they become less likely to successfully choose a mate. The findings reveal how cognitive limits may influence mating behavior not only in treefrogs, but also across the animal kingdom. title: Patrick Heide Contemporary Art opens summer group show Woven Dialogues
summary: Patrick Heide Contemporary Art is presenting the summer group exhibition, entitled Woven Dialogues. Woven Dialogues brings together five artists, Kate Terry, Bonolo Kavula, Raphaella Pester, Dillwyn Smith and Defne Tesal, whose practices, though geographically and culturally distinct, share a deep commitment to materiality and the expressive possibilities of textiles and fibre. The exhibition stages a series of encounters: between intimate, hand-built objects and site-specific interventions; between natural pigments and industrially coloured found materials; and between raw, undyed earth tones and vibrant neon hues. Kate Terry (b. 1976, Canada) opens the conversation with a bold spatial intervention. title: The Cleveland Museum of Art hosts the 2026 Cleveland Silent Film Festival and Colloquium
summary: The Cleveland Museum of Art welcomes the return of the Cleveland Silent Film Festival and Colloquium to Gartner Auditorium this September for four days to celebrate the expressive power of early cinema. Each year, a carefully curated selection of silent films is paired with live musical accompaniment by renowned specialists creating unforgettable cinematic experiences. “The Silent Film Festival gives audiences a rare opportunity to see these films on a large screen with local and nationally based musicians playing exceptional music,” said Gabe Pollack, director of performing arts. “This year’s film selections have something for every type of film lover. title: Over 200 works by Frederic Church digitized for public access in new online portal
summary: The Olana Partnership and the New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP) announce the largest launch to date of public online collections for Olana State Historic Site on August 17, 2026. Upon its launch, this resource will feature over 200 records of artwork by the artist Frederic Church, Olana’s creator, and is an important part of the year-long Frederic Church 200 initiative led by The Olana Partnership to mark the 200th anniversary of Church’s birth. The work undertaken to develop this digital collections resource for Olana is made possible by a major, multi-year grant from the Henry Luce Foundation. Olana is the most intact artist’s environments in the United States, with a vast collection encompassing over 90,000 objects. title: Museum Angewandte Kunst to open exhibition on graphic design's influence
summary: Graphic design is everywhere, from the packaging on supermarket shelves and the interfaces on our phones to advertising, signage and the systems that help us navigate public space. Yet much of its influence goes unnoticed. A new exhibition at the Museum Angewandte Kunst in Frankfurt sets out to make that influence visible. Opening August 20, On Display. How Graphic Design Shapes Us looks at the ways graphic design affects how people perceive information, understand the world and make decisions. Bringing together work by Robin Coenen and Danielle Rosales, Aline Bavier and Sophia Becker, and Anja Kaiser and Rebecca Stephany, the exhibition considers the social and political power of design at a moment of rapid technological and cultural change.
